extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of aesthetics/philosophy of art; art critics and theorists
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts Kant's criteria for what constitutes beautiful art, the faculties involved (Imagination, Understanding, Judgement, Spirit, Taste), the taxonomy of the arts, and evaluative hierarchies among art forms. Focuses on how to recognise genius, aesthetic ideas, and failures such as mannerism or mere gratification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautiful art as purposiveness without purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty in art is the form of purposiveness that appears in the object though without any definite purpose (i.e. purposiveness without being sought as a purpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art ought to present purposiveness in its form so that judgement finds it purposive for our faculties although not for any external purpose; this distinguishes beautiful art from mere useful design or moral treatises which may show form but are not called works of beautiful art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spirit (the animating principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spirit is the animating principle of the mind that puts the mental powers purposively into play and strengthens them in exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A work can be neat and tasteful yet 'without spirit' — spirit is what enlivens a poem, history, discourse or conversation; the presence of spirit indicates that the work affords a self-sustaining play of imagination and thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetical Idea
rubrics_metrics.description: An aesthetical Idea is a representation of the Imagination which occasions much thought without any definite concept being adequate to it; it cannot be completely expressed by language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetical Ideas are the content that quickens thought without being capturable by concepts; they are the counterpart of rational Ideas and are central to poetry and other arts that aim to arouse free imaginative thought (examples: poetical presentations of eternity, death, fame).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetical attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes are imaginative representations (e.g. Jupiter’s eagle) that do not correspond to logical attributes of a concept but expand the Imagination by suggesting a multiplicity of kindred representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributes serve as substitutes for rational presentation, enliven the mind, and supply undeveloped material that stimulates further imaginative thought; they function across painting, sculpture, poetry and rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genius (faculty-combination and originality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius is a natural, exemplary originality arising from the free employment of Imagination and Understanding; it is a talent for art (not science) by which aesthetical Ideas are found for a given concept and expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genius presupposes a definite concept of the product, a relation of Imagination to Understanding, and the production of unsought aesthetic purposiveness. Its products give new, inimitable rules for art and cannot be taught by science or mere industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics/conditions of genius (fourfold)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1) Genius is a talent for Art not Science. 2) It presupposes a definite concept (purpose) and representation of material (intuition), linking Imagination and Understanding. 3) It shows itself in enunciation of aesthetical Ideas rather than the mere accomplishment of a concept. 4) Its free, undesigned purposiveness arises from natural disposition that rules cannot produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four points serve as diagnostic criteria for attributing a work to genius rather than to schooling, technique, or rule-following.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression (spirit) as communicative talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of genius is the talent to express the ineffable state of mind caused by aesthetical Ideas — seizing the quickly passing play of Imagination and unifying it in an original concept communicable to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expressive talent (spirit) is distinct from mere imaginative wealth: it is what makes subjective purposiveness universally communicable (§ on spirit and genius).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste as discipline of genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Taste (Judgement) is the discipline or training of genius, clipping and polishing Imagination while giving guidance where and how far it may extend to remain purposive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taste brings clearness and order to imaginative abundance, rendering Ideas susceptible of universal assent and cultural transmission; it should be privileged over abundance when conflict arises (i.e. judgement will sacrifice freedom of imagination rather than undermine understanding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary faculties for beautiful art
rubrics_metrics.description: Beautiful art requires the joint presence of Imagination, Understanding, Spirit, and Taste (Judgement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imagination supplies ideas; Understanding supplies the concept/purpose; Spirit expresses the ineffable; Taste regulates and disciplines — their proper interplay constitutes the groundwork of beautiful art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genius vs imitation / exemplary originality
rubrics_metrics.description: A genius's product is exemplary — not to be imitated wholesale but to awaken originality in others; imitation that copies deformities or peculiarities is mere aping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genius should be 'followed' by inspiring originality, not 'copied'; school formation from a genius leads to methodical rules, but unthinking aping (copying everything including flaws) is condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mannerism and peculiarity as faults
rubrics_metrics.description: Mannerism is aping of mere peculiarity or ostentatious singularity that is founded on singularity rather than the Idea; it separates the artist from others without being exemplary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mannerism manifests as affected, contorted behaviour or style aimed at differentiating oneself rather than expressing the Idea — it signals a bungler rather than a genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art must be free (avoid studied anxiousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beautiful art must be free in a double sense: free play of Imagination and not a product of anxious study or deliberate mechanical procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the combination of faculties appears contrived or rule-bound, it fails as beautiful art; beautiful art is not tradesmanlike or measurable against commercial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetoric vs Poetry (arts of speech distinction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetoric is the art of carrying on serious business of Understanding as if it were free play of Imagination (persuasion), whereas poetry conducts free play of Imagination as if it were serious business of Understanding (entertaining play that enriches Understanding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The orator promises business but provides entertainment; the poet promises play but supplies material worthy of understanding. Rhetoric as persuasion (ars oratoria) is dialectical and can be objectionable when used to deceive.

rubrics_metrics.name: The arts of speech must avoid deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetoric used for persuasion can deprive audiences of freedom by charming them before judgement, and is unfit for law courts or the pulpit; poetry declares itself as play and thus avoids deceit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eloquence and clear presentation of maxims are preferable for serious matters; the machinery of persuasion should not be used to beautify or hide vice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division principle of the beautiful arts (three kinds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beautiful arts are divided analogically to modes of expression in speech — word, deportment, and tone — yielding three kinds: arts of speech, formative arts, and the art of the play of sensations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This taxonomy is recommended as convenient and maps to rhetoric/poetry, sculpture/painting/architecture, and music/colour-art respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formative arts: plastic (sensible truth) vs painting (sensible illusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formative arts either express Ideas in sensible truth (Plastic: sculpture, architecture) or in sensible illusion (Painting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plastic arts present figures cognisable by sight and touch; painting presents only the appearance and illusory extension. Architecture importantly involves use/utility, while sculpture focuses on expression as corporeal presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between sculpture and architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: Sculpture presents corporeal concepts as they might exist in nature (expression of aesthetical Ideas); architecture presents concepts possible only through art and is determined by an intended use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architecture's chief point is the utility of an artistic object, which limits aesthetical Ideas; sculpture aims at aesthetic expression without functional purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Painting subdivided: depiction vs arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting (as sensible illusion) divides into (a) the beautiful depicting of nature (painting proper) and (b) the beautiful arrangement of its products (landscape gardening).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wide sense of painting includes room decoration, tapestry, bric-a-brac, garments etc. — objects meant merely to be looked at and to entertain Imagination without definite purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art of the beautiful play of sensations (music and colour)
rubrics_metrics.description: This art concerns proportion of sensory disposition (tone) and divides into music (hearing) and the art of colour (sight); its objects may be pleasant sensations or constitute a beautiful play of sensations depending on judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is debate whether colours/tones are mere pleasant sensations or forms subject to judgement; mathematical proportion (relations of vibrations) provides a ground for judging musical form, even though the aesthetical Idea is not a determinate concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical/formal condition in music
rubrics_metrics.description: Music's beauty rests on proportion (relation between number of vibrations) which allows judgement on harmony and melody even absent determinate concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematics is the conditio sine qua non that prevents musical impressions from destroying one another and allows harmonious proportion, though the cultural/charming effect of music is not reducible to mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanence vs transitory effect of arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Formative arts produce permanent impressions (serve as concepts/vehicles for cultivation); music produces transitory impressions and is more about enjoyment than culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formative arts can be recalled and serve long-term cultivation of higher cognitive powers; music requires constant change and does not bear frequent repetition without weariness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy of the arts (aesthetic worth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry ranks highest among the arts for expanding the mind and setting Imagination at liberty; formative arts (especially painting) outrank music in cultural worth; music has lower worth insofar as it mainly plays with sensations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry offers aesthetical Ideas that strengthen thought and schematize the supersensible; painting penetrates further into Ideas among formative arts; music is highest among pleasurable arts but lower in fostering lasting cognitive culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Different arts may be combined in a single product (e.g., theatre combines rhetoric and pictorial presentation; song combines poetry and music; opera combines poetry, music, and theatrical presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combination can make art more artistic but not necessarily more beautiful — cross-satisfaction types can conflict. Essential element across combinations is the form purposive for judgement that cultivates the spirit with Ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Danger of mere gratification (pleasure without cultivation)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a distinction between what satisfies in the act of judging and what gratifies (pleasure in sensation); gratification often relates to bodily well-being and may not contribute to cultivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the beautiful arts are not linked with moral/Reasoned Ideas they risk becoming mere distraction that leaves no lasting benefit; beauty tied to moral ideas gives self-sufficing satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art should not obtrude on others (music example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some arts (e.g., music) may impose themselves on others (like a pervasive scent) because they cannot be avoided by turning away; visual arts do not do this as easily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the social effect and intrusiveness of art forms when judging appropriateness; music's ubiquity can be a point against its urbane worth in certain settings.
